mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 4.0% (FEDFUNDS ≤ 4.0%) consistently correlates with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to accommodative monetary policy reducing discount rates for equity valuation.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS ≤ 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% (UNRATE > 4.5%) triggers negative S&P 500 5-day returns due to deteriorating labor market conditions reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) and housing starts (HOUST < 1300) signal concurrent manufacturing and residential sector contraction, producing negative S&P 500 60-day returns due to reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100 AND HOUST < 1300.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3.5% annualized), the S&P 500 experiences negative 20-day returns due to reduced liquidity and increased risk aversion from aggressive central bank policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3.5% (annualized).

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment levels above 150,000 (PAYEMS > 150,000) consistently predict positive S&P 500 20-day returns due to robust labor market conditions supporting consumer spending and corporate profitability.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS > 150,000.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1250 (HOUST < 1250) triggers negative S&P 500 5-day returns due to weakened residential construction activity reducing consumer confidence and economic growth momentum.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST < 1250.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in real GDP (GDPC1 < 2.0% annualized) and retail sales (RSAFS < 700,000) signal weakening consumer demand, producing negative S&P 500 60-day returns due to reduced corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 < 2.0% AND RSAFS < 700,000.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 100 (INDPRO < 100) triggers negative S&P 500 20-day returns due to manufacturing sector weakness reducing corporate earnings and equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100.
